newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Pujol says wants more tax powers in future.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Pujol says wants more tax powers in future.

text.p: Jordi Pujol, leader of the Spanish government's Catalan political allies, says he will carry on backing the ruling Popular Party (PP) but wants tax concessions for his region in return.

Pujol, who holds the balance of power in parliament, told reporters on Thursday night that dialogue had broken down between the government and the Catalans on a number of issues, singling out health spending and regional investment as "dark areas" which needed to be addressed.
He was speaking after a meeting with Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar which lasted more than three hours.
"Some things have been fixed and others, no," Pujol said. "In a collaboration of this type there are always frictions, misunderstandings or disagreements."

Relations between the administration and the Catalans have been strained since the government last week conceded powers to the Basque country and Navarre to collect special taxes on alcohol, cigarettes and fossil fuels.
Pujol said he would not demand the same powers for his region yet but would do so "maybe within one or two years".

Government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez brushed over any conflict, saying that there was agreement on broad issues such as Spain's ambition to join a single European Union currency and that the personal relationship between Pujol and Aznar was healthy.

But Public Administration Minister Mariano Rajoy signalled storm clouds on the horizon when he told a radio interviewer that the government would refuse to cede control of special taxes to Pujol in 1998.
